models.name: erp_hrm_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for tracking pre-authentication visitors identified by device fingerprint.

Guests represent unauthenticated users who have not yet signed into the platform or do not have an account. The guest actor represents the initial state of all users before they complete authentication. Guests have no identity within the platform until they either create a new account through sign-up or authenticate with an existing account through login.

Once authenticated, they transition to the member actor status. This table provides the foundation for session tracking and enables the platform to maintain state for browsing visitors.

plainFields.name: fingerprint
plainFields.description: Device fingerprint used to identify and track unique visitors before authentication. Provides a consistent identity for session tracking and visitor analytics across page visits.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was soft-deleted. Used for cleanup of expired guest records.

models.name: erp_hrm_guest_sessions
models.description: Session tracking for guest actor temporary access. Records connection context (IP, href, referrer) and expiration for pre-authentication visitors browsing the platform before signup. Each guest can have multiple concurrent sessions across devices.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest actor who owns this session. {@link erp_hrm_guests.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client connection. Used for security audit and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL path the guest accessed. Records the entry point or current location in the application.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header indicating where the guest came from. Nullable as referrer may not be present.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Marks the beginning of the guest's visit.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Required for security - sessions must have a defined lifetime.

models.name: erp_hrm_members
models.description:
Authenticated user accounts that serve as the primary identity for accessing the ERP HRM platform. Each member is uniquely identified by their email address and authenticates using password credentials.

Members maintain a global profile (display name, avatar image, phone number) that is shared across all organizations they belong to. When logging in, members select an organization context, and all subsequent actions are scoped to that organization.

This is the root actor entity - referenced by session tables (erp_hrm_member_sessions, erp_hrm_member_password_resets) and employee membership records (erp_hrm_employees) that link members to specific organizations.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address serving as the primary identifier for authentication. Must be unique across the entire platform - no two users can share the same email. Used for login and organization invitations.

plainFields.name: password
plainFields.description: Hashed password credential for account authentication. Users create this password during registration and can change it through account settings. Stored securely using industry-standard hashing algorithms.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name that identifies the member to others within organizations. Appears in all interactions such as viewing employees, timelogs, or task assignments. Required field shared across all organizational memberships.

plainFields.name: avatar_image
plainFields.description: Optional URL to the member's avatar image for visual identification. Helps team members recognize each other in collaborative contexts. Shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Optional contact phone number stored as text. Allows organizations to reach the member if needed. Shared across all organizational memberships.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created. Records the initial sign-up moment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated. Updated on profile changes or password changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted. Null for active accounts. When deleted, the member can no longer authenticate or access organizations, but their historical data (timelogs, timesheets) is preserved.

models.name: erp_hrm_member_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens for authenticated members supporting organization context switching. Each session tracks the member's authentication state, connection metadata (IP address, current URL, referrer), and currently selected organization context. Sessions expire based on the expired_at timestamp and can be refreshed. The organization_id field allows members to switch between organizations they belong to without re-authentication.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_member_id
foreignFields.description: The authenticated member this session belongs to. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_organization_id
foreignFields.description: The currently selected organization context for this session. Nullable because the member may not have selected an organization yet, or may have been removed from all organizations. Members can switch organizations without logging out by updating this field. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client that initiated this session. Used for security logging and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL path the member was accessing when the session was created or last active. Used for session tracking and security auditing.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The HTTP Referrer header value when the session was created. Used for tracking session origin and security analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created (login time).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was last updated (e.g., when switching organization context or refreshing tokens).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires. Sessions must be refreshed before this time to remain valid. Security-critical field - session tokens are invalid after this timestamp.

models.name: erp_hrm_member_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for member account recovery. Stores temporary tokens with expiration that allow members to reset their password when they cannot authenticate. Each token is valid for a limited time and can only be used once. A member may have multiple reset tokens if they request multiple resets without completing the recovery flow.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who requested the password reset. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Hashed password reset token. This is a secure hash of the actual token sent to the user. The token must be unique across all reset requests to prevent collision attacks.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset was requested. Used for audit trail and to calculate token age.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. Tokens become invalid after this time for security purposes. Must be set at creation time - there is no indefinite reset token.

models.name: erp_hrm_organizations
models.description:
Primary tenant containers in the multi-tenant ERP platform. Each organization operates as an independent tenant with complete data isolation from other organizations.

Organizations store identity attributes (name, description, logo) and operational configuration (currency, timezone, fiscal start month). The owner reference tracks the user who created the organization. All organization-scoped business entities (employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, etc.) belong to exactly one organization.

Data isolation is enforced at the application layer through organization context scoping. When users belong to multiple organizations, they select an active organization context, and all subsequent operations are scoped to that organization.

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: The user who created and owns this organization. Has full administrative rights including organization deletion. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Organization display name used as the primary identifier throughout the platform interface.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional additional context about the organization's purpose, nature, or business focus.

plainFields.name: logo_image
plainFields.description: Optional URL to the organization's logo image for visual branding. Displayed in the organization interface to help members identify their current organization context.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Designated currency for financial operations within the organization. Supported values include USD, EUR, KRW, and other common international currencies. All monetary values associated with the organization use this currency.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Organization's preferred timezone for time tracking and reporting. Affects how dates and times display for all members within that organization context.

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description: Month number (1-12) when the organization's fiscal year begins. Impacts financial reporting and budget tracking features, allowing organizations to align reporting periods with fiscal calendars.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was soft-deleted. Null if the organization is active. Soft deletion preserves data for potential recovery while removing the organization from active operations.

models.name: erp_hrm_roles
models.description: Organization-scoped role definitions that determine employee permissions within an organization. Each role contains a name and a collection of permissions assigned through the {@link erp_hrm_role_permissions} table. The three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are protected from deletion via the is_builtin flag and are automatically created when a new organization is established. Custom roles can be created by organization owners with the org:manage permission to define custom permission combinations. Role names must be unique within each organization scope.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization that owns this role. All roles belong to a specific organization for multi-tenant data isolation. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The display name of the role within the organization. Built-in roles have fixed names (Owner, Manager, Employee) while custom roles can have any name chosen by the organization owner. Must be unique within the same organization.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description: Whether this role is a built-in system role that cannot be deleted. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are created automatically when an organization is established and have predefined permission sets. Custom roles created by users have this set to false.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this role was created. Built-in roles are created at organization creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this role was last modified. Custom roles can be edited by organization owners.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this role was soft-deleted. Built-in roles cannot be deleted. Custom roles can only be deleted if no employees are assigned to them.

models.name: erp_hrm_role_permissions
models.description:
Permission assignments for roles, defining what actions users with a specific role can perform.

Each permission record grants a specific capability to a role. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have their permissions populated automatically, while custom roles have permissions assigned by organization owners.

Available permissions include:
- org:manage — Edit organization settings
- employee:manage — Add, edit, deactivate employees
- employee:view — View employee list and details
- project:manage — Create, edit, delete projects and tasks
- project:view — View projects and tasks
- time:manage — Edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- time:approve — Approve or reject timesheets
- time:view_all — View all employees' timelogs and timesheets
- report:view — View organization reports

This table is always accessed through the parent {@link erp_hrm_roles} entity and is not managed independently by users.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_role_id
foreignFields.description: The role that this permission belongs to. {@link erp_hrm_roles.id}

plainFields.name: permission
plainFields.description: The permission code representing a specific capability. Values include: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission was assigned to the role.

models.name: erp_hrm_employees
models.description:
User membership records within organizations, establishing the bridge between user accounts and organizational access. Each employee represents a user's employment relationship with a specific organization, including role assignment for permission control, optional department affiliation, employment classification, and activation status.

An employee is uniquely identified by the combination of user account and organization—each user can have at most one employee record per organization, but may belong to multiple organizations through separate employee records. The assigned role determines what actions the employee can perform within the organization.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link erp_hrm_members} (user account) - the global user identity
- Belongs to {@link erp_hrm_organizations} - the organizational context
- Assigned one {@link erp_hrm_roles} - determines permissions
- Optionally assigned to {@link erp_hrm_departments} - organizational structure
- Has many {@link erp_hrm_contracts} - employment history
- Has many {@link erp_hrm_project_members} - project assignments
- Has one {@link erp_hrm_timers} - active time tracking session
- Has many {@link erp_hrm_timelogs} - recorded work sessions
- Has many {@link erp_hrm_timesheets} - weekly timesheet submissions

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user account who owns this employee record. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the organization this employee belongs to. All employee data is scoped to this organization. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_role_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the role assigned to this employee, determining their permissions within the organization. Each employee has exactly one role at any time. {@link erp_hrm_roles.id}

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_department_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to the department this employee is assigned to. Employees without department assignment are considered unassigned for organizational purposes. {@link erp_hrm_departments.id}

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Optional job title or position within the organization, such as 'Software Engineer' or 'Marketing Manager'. This is distinct from the system role and reflects the employee's official designation.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Employment classification within the organization. Valid values: 'full_time' for standard full-time hours, 'part_time' for reduced hours, 'contractor' for external workers, 'intern' for temporary training positions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Activation status of the employee record. Active employees can log time and submit timesheets. Deactivated employees cannot perform these actions but their historical data is preserved. Valid values: 'active', 'deactivated'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee record was soft-deleted. Null for active records.

models.name: erp_hrm_departments
models.description:
Organizational units within each organization for grouping employees by function, team, or area of responsibility. Supports single-level hierarchy through optional parent department reference, where a department with a parent cannot itself have children. Department names must be unique within the same organization. When a department is deleted, employees previously assigned to it have their department reference cleared.

Departments provide the organizational structure that enables categorizing employees by their functional areas (e.g., Engineering, Marketing, Human Resources, Finance). The hierarchy feature allows for both granular team-level departments (e.g., Backend Development as child of Engineering) and high-level organizational views in reporting.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization this department belongs to. Departments are organization-scoped and data-isolated per tenant. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent department reference for single-level hierarchy. When set, this department is a child team within the parent department. A department with a parent cannot itself have children (enforced by application logic). {@link erp_hrm_departments.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The department name that serves as its primary identifier within the organization. Must be unique across all departments in the same organization. Used in lists, reports, and assignment interfaces.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional additional context about the department's purpose, scope, or the types of work performed by employees assigned to that department.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, the department is considered deleted but preserved for audit and data integrity. Employees assigned to deleted departments have their reference cleared.

models.name: erp_hrm_contracts
models.description:
Employee employment contracts tracking pay rates, working hours, and validity periods for historical and active employment records.

Each employee can have multiple contracts maintained as historical records throughout their tenure, but only one contract can be active at any given time. An active contract is identified by having a start date that has passed and either a null end date (ongoing) or an end date in the future.

Past contracts with end dates in the past are immutable and serve as permanent historical records for payroll and audit purposes. When a new contract is created for an employee with an existing active contract, the system automatically ends the previous contract.

This table supports the contract management workflow where users with employee management permission can create new contracts and edit active contracts, while past contracts remain locked for compliance.

Key relationships:
- Each contract belongs to exactly one {@link erp_hrm_employees} via erp_hrm_employee_id
- Multiple contracts per employee form an employment history chain

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who owns this employment contract. Each employee can have multiple contracts over time as historical records, with at most one contract active at any given time. {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The date when employment under this contract begins. This field is required and cannot be changed once set. When a new contract is created for an employee with an existing active contract, the system uses this start date to determine when the previous contract should end.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: The date when employment under this contract terminates. When null, the contract is considered ongoing without a predetermined conclusion. When specified and in the future, the contract is active. When specified and in the past, the contract is a historical record that cannot be modified.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: The employee's compensation amount as a numeric value. The interpretation depends on the pay_period field (e.g., hourly rate for hourly pay period, monthly salary for monthly pay period).

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: The payment frequency for this contract. Valid values: 'hourly' (compensation per hour), 'daily' (compensation per day), 'weekly' (compensation per week), 'monthly' (compensation per month). The pay_rate value must be interpreted in conjunction with this field.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: The expected weekly commitment in hours for this contract. For example, a standard full-time contract might specify 40 hours per week. This value is used for budget tracking and capacity planning.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional additional context, special terms, or conditions for this contract. Can include information about benefits, allowances, or specific employment arrangements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract record was created. Used for audit trail and historical ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract record was last modified. For past contracts (end_date in the past), this field will not change as edits are prohibited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft delete. When set, the contract is marked as deleted but retained for historical and audit purposes. Contracts are typically not hard-deleted to preserve employment history.

models.name: erp_hrm_projects
models.description:
Work containers within organizations that group tasks and track time. Projects are created by users with project:manage permission and can be filtered by status. Active projects can receive timelogs; archived or completed projects preserve existing timelogs but cannot receive new ones. Each project has optional budget hours for tracking estimated work against actual time logged.

Projects serve as the primary organizational unit for work management, with members assigned through the {@link erp_hrm_project_members} junction table. Project leads (members with lead role) can manage tasks within their assigned projects.

{@link erp_hrm_organizations} owns projects. {@link erp_hrm_tasks} belong to projects. {@link erp_hrm_project_members} assign employees to projects.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization that owns this project. Projects are strictly isolated by organization. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Project name. Required for identification and display in project lists.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the project's purpose and scope. Optional field for additional context.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Hex color code for UI display (e.g., #FF5733). Required for visual identification in dashboards and project lists.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Project lifecycle status. Active projects can receive new timelogs. Archived or completed projects preserve existing data but cannot receive new timelogs. Valid values: 'active', 'archived', 'completed'.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description: Total estimated hours for the project. Optional field used for budget tracking and utilization reports. Projects without budget hours are excluded from budget utilization reports.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional project start date for scheduling and planning purposes.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Optional project end date for scheduling and planning purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Projects can only be deleted if they have no associated timelogs.

models.name: erp_hrm_project_members
models.description: Junction table establishing many-to-many relationships between employees and projects with role differentiation. Each record represents a project membership with an assigned role (member or project-lead). Project leads have elevated permissions to manage tasks within their assigned project. This enables employees to participate in multiple projects with different roles per project. Managed by users with project:manage permission. References {@link erp_hrm_employees} for membership and {@link erp_hrm_projects} for project assignment.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee assigned to this project. Each employee can be assigned to multiple projects. References {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_project_id
foreignFields.description: The project this membership belongs to. Each project can have multiple members with various roles. References {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: The role assigned to this employee for this project. 'member' is a standard participant who can log time on the project. 'project_lead' has elevated permissions to manage tasks within the project including creating, editing, and assigning tasks.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was soft-deleted. Null if the membership is active.

models.name: erp_hrm_tasks
models.description:
Work items within projects representing specific units of work that can be tracked, assigned, and monitored.

Each task belongs to a project and has a required title with optional description. Tasks progress through four status values: open (new and waiting), in-progress (actively being worked on), completed (work finished), and closed (no longer actively tracked). Priority levels indicate urgency: low (deferrable), medium (normal workflow), high (prompt attention needed), and urgent (critical and immediate action required).

Tasks support one level of nesting through an optional parent task reference, allowing larger tasks to be decomposed into subtasks. Employees assigned to the project can be designated as responsible for completing the task. Estimated hours capture anticipated effort, and due dates establish expected completion timelines.

The task lifecycle supports archival closure rather than hard deletion when timelogs are associated. Task status changes are recorded as immutable history entries in {@link erp_hrm_task_histories} for audit trail purposes.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Project that this task belongs to. Tasks are always associated with a project context. {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee assigned to complete this task. Must be a project member. Nullable indicates unassigned tasks. {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_task_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task for subtask relationships. Supports one level of nesting only. A task with a parent is a subtask; parent tasks cannot themselves be subtasks. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Brief descriptive title of the task indicating the work to be accomplished.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description providing additional context and requirements for completing the task.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the task: 'open' (new, waiting to be worked on), 'in-progress' (actively being worked on), 'completed' (work finished), or 'closed' (no longer actively tracked).

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level indicating urgency: 'low' (deferrable), 'medium' (normal workflow), 'high' (prompt attention), or 'urgent' (critical immediate action).

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: Anticipated effort in hours required to complete the task, used for planning and tracking.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Expected completion date for the task, establishing the timeline deadline.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was soft-deleted. Tasks with associated timelogs cannot be hard-deleted and are closed instead.

models.name: erp_hrm_task_histories
models.description: Immutable audit trail of task status transitions recording when and how tasks progress through their lifecycle. Each entry captures a single status change event, preserving the previous status, new status, the timestamp of the change, and the member who performed the action. Task history entries serve as a transparent record for understanding task progression and accountability, allowing stakeholders to track how and when work items moved through stages such as open, in-progress, completed, and closed.

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: The task whose status changed. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who performed the status change. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: The task status before this change. Possible values: 'open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed'.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The task status after this change. Possible values: 'open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status change occurred.

models.name: erp_hrm_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries recording work sessions performed by employees. Each timelog captures the date when work occurred, duration in minutes, the project worked on, an optional task assignment, optional description of work performed, and a billable flag indicating invoicing eligibility.

Timelogs are owned by employees and can be included in weekly timesheets for approval. Once a timesheet is approved, all included timelogs become locked and cannot be modified or deleted. Timelogs can be filtered by date range, project, task, and billable status.

Related entities: {@link erp_hrm_employees} (owner), {@link erp_hrm_projects} (required assignment), {@link erp_hrm_tasks} (optional), {@link erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs} (junction for timesheet inclusion).

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who logged this time entry. Each employee can only create timelogs for themselves. {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: The project this time was logged against. The employee must be assigned to this project before logging time. {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: The optional task this time was logged against. If specified, the task must belong to the selected project. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description: The date when the work was performed. Required for all timelogs and used for weekly timesheet aggregation and date range filtering.

plainFields.name: duration
plainFields.description: The total time spent in minutes. Records how long the work session lasted. Required for all timelogs.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional notes documenting what work was performed during the recorded time. Allows employees to provide context for their time entries.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this time entry should be considered billable for invoicing purposes. Defaults to true for new timelogs. Non-billable timelogs represent internal work or administrative tasks.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was soft-deleted. Null for active timelogs.

models.name: erp_hrm_timesheets
models.description: Weekly timesheet aggregations (Monday to Sunday) for approval workflow. Each timesheet represents a collection of timelogs for a specific week, owned by an employee, and progresses through draft/submitted/approved/rejected status states. Submitted timesheets require manager approval and become locked upon approval. Rejected timesheets return to draft status for revision. Supports filtering by status and date range with pagination.

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who owns this timesheet and whose timelogs are aggregated. {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: User who reviewed (approved or rejected) this timesheet. Set when status transitions to approved or rejected. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: Start date of the timesheet week (Monday). This defines the beginning of the weekly period being aggregated.

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description: End date of the timesheet week (Sunday). This defines the end of the weekly period being aggregated.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current workflow status of the timesheet. Valid values: 'draft' (editable by employee), 'submitted' (awaiting approval), 'approved' (locked, cannot be modified), 'rejected' (returned to draft for revision).

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description: Total hours calculated from all included timelogs. Sum of duration_minutes/60 for all linked timelogs.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for approval. Set when status transitions from draft to submitted.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was reviewed (approved or rejected). Set when status transitions to approved or rejected.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for why the timesheet was rejected. Required when status is 'rejected' and a manager provides feedback for the employee to address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Set when the timesheet is deleted but preserved for audit purposes.

models.name: erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs
models.description:
Junction table connecting timesheets to their included timelogs, enabling the many-to-many relationship between weekly timesheet aggregations and individual time entries. This table supports draft management where employees can add or remove timelogs from a draft timesheet before submission. Once a timesheet is approved, the timelog associations become locked and cannot be modified, preventing edits to the underlying timelogs.

Each association represents one timelog entry that is included in a specific timesheet for a particular week. The relationship is managed through the timesheet lifecycle: draft timesheets allow modifications, while approved timesheets enforce immutability for both the timesheet and its associated timelogs.

**Related Entities:**
- {@link erp_hrm_timesheets} — Parent timesheet aggregations
- {@link erp_hrm_timelogs} — Individual time entry records

foreignFields.name: timesheet_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the timesheet that includes this timelog. Part of the timesheet-timelog association for weekly time aggregation. {@link erp_hrm_timesheets.id}

foreignFields.name: timelog_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the timelog entry included in this timesheet. Each timelog can be included in at most one timesheet per week. {@link erp_hrm_timelogs.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet-timelog association was created. Records when the timelog was added to the timesheet.

models.name: erp_hrm_timers
models.description:
Real-time tracking sessions for employees to record work time as it happens. Each timer captures the start timestamp when tracking begins, the project being worked on, and optional task and description. An employee can have at most one active timer at any time - this constraint is enforced at the application layer. When stopped, the timer duration is calculated and converted to a timelog entry. Timers can also be discarded without creating a timelog. Historical timer records are preserved through soft deletion.

The timer enables real-time productivity tracking and automatic duration calculation, supporting flexible work recording without requiring employees to remember exact start/end times.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who owns and started this timer. Each employee can have at most one active timer at any given time. {@link erp_hrm_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_project_id
foreignFields.description: The project being tracked by this timer. Must be a project the employee is assigned to as a project member. {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional task within the project being tracked. If specified, must belong to the same project and the employee must be a project member. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timer was started. This marks the beginning of the work session and is used to calculate duration when the timer is stopped.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional notes describing what work is being performed during this tracking session. Can be edited while the timer is running.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer record was created. Coincides with started_at for new timers.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer record was last modified, such as when editing the description or project/task assignment.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was stopped or discarded. A null value indicates the timer is currently active. Stopped timers convert to timelog entries, while discarded timers simply end without creating a timelog.

models.name: erp_hrm_invitations
models.description:
Pending invitations to join an organization, tracking the invited email address, assigned role, and invitation status. When an existing user's email is invited, they are immediately added to the organization. When a new user's email is invited, a pending invitation is created that activates when the user signs up with that email address. Authorized users with employee:manage permission can create and cancel invitations.

Each invitation establishes a connection between an email address and an organization, with an assigned role that will be granted upon acceptance. The invitation lifecycle flows from pending to either accepted (when the user joins) or cancelled (when revoked by an administrator).

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization to which the recipient is being invited. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: The role that will be assigned to the employee upon acceptance. {@link erp_hrm_roles.id}

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: The email address of the invited person. Must be a valid email format. When a user signs up with this email, any matching pending invitations trigger automatic organization membership.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the invitation. 'pending' indicates awaiting user registration, 'accepted' indicates the user has been added to the organization, 'cancelled' indicates the invitation was revoked by an authorized user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was last modified, such as when status changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was soft-deleted (cancelled). Null for active invitations.

models.name: erp_hrm_activity_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit trail entries capturing significant organizational actions for compliance and accountability. Each entry records the timestamp, user performer, action type, target entity, organization context, and optional details.

Activity logs are append-only records that cannot be modified after creation. They support filtering by action type, user, and date range for audit and reporting purposes. Users with org:manage permission can view the full activity log within their organization.

The polymorphic entity reference (entity_type + entity_id) allows tracking actions across different entity types including employees, contracts, projects, tasks, timesheets, and roles without creating circular foreign key references.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The user who performed the action. {@link erp_hrm_members.id}

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization context in which the action occurred. All activity logs are organization-scoped for data isolation. {@link erp_hrm_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: The type of action performed. Valid values include: employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, role_changed.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: The type of entity that was the target of the action. Valid values: employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: The unique identifier of the target entity. Combined with entity_type to form a polymorphic reference.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Additional context about the action, such as old and new values for status changes or rejection reasons. Stored as text for flexibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was performed. Activity logs are immutable after creation.
